newsitem.title: UK: Boeing to seek close links with British Aerospace.
newsitem.headline: Boeing to seek close links with British Aerospace.

text.p: U.S. aircraft maker Boeing Co wants to increase its ties with British Aerospace Plc (Bae) and other international aerospace companies, a report in the Financial Times said on Wednesday.
In an interview with the paper, Boeing chairman Philip Condit said he wanted Boeing to grow internationally so it was no longer seen as an American group.
"I believe we are moving towards an era of global markets and global companies," he told the paper. "I think it is advantageous that your workforce, your executive corps, reflect that."
The paper said Condit saw Bae as a possible partner on the planned U.S. Joint Strike Fighter.
The British firm unsuccessfully bid for the fighter contract last year in a consortium including McDonnell Douglas.
No one at Bae was immediately available for comment on the interview.

The Financial Times pointed out that Bae was already a partner of McDonnell on the Harrier jump jet, while Boeing was a subcontractor to Bae to provide replacements for Britain's fleet of Nimrod maritime patrol aircraft.
